concrete_examples.description: In NetHack, procedural generation is implemented through algorithms that create the dungeon layout, including the arrangement of rooms, corridors, and special features, ensuring that each playthrough offers a unique configuration while maintaining gameplay balance. This randomness extends to item placement, enemy types, and even the generation of special quests, contributing to the game's high replayability.

In broguece, procedural generation is implemented through algorithms that create unique dungeon layouts, item placements, and enemy spawn points for each playthrough, ensuring that no two runs are the same and enhancing replayability.

In 'Crawl', procedural generation is utilized to create diverse dungeon layouts and enemy placements, ensuring that each playthrough offers a unique experience. This mechanism allows for varying strategies and exploration paths, significantly enhancing replayability.

In cataclysm-bn, procedural generation is utilized to create a vast, open world filled with dynamically generated cities, towns, and wilderness areas, ensuring that each playthrough presents a unique map layout and resource distribution. This system allows players to encounter different challenges and environments in every game session, enhancing replayability.

definition: A game mechanic where game content (levels, items, monsters, maps) is generated algorithmically rather than hand-designed. This creates unique playthroughs and high replayability but reduces designer control over specific experiences.
exclusion_criteria: Cosmetic randomization that doesn't affect gameplay
inclusion_criteria: Game levels or maps are generated by algorithms
Each playthrough produces different content layouts
Content generation uses random seeds with deterministic algorithms
Player cannot predict exact layout before exploration
title: Procedural Generation
